answer: The delta detector writes to ridge, and jade reveals every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, and thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 39 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 104 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 40 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
